title: No Records Found — Why SASSA Cannot Find Your Application
description: SASSA status 'No Records Found' does not mean you were declined. It usually means the ID or phone number used did not match an application. Here is how to fix it.

seo.metaTitle: SASSA 'No Records Found' Status — Causes & Fix (2026)
seo.metaDescription: Why SASSA returns 'No Records Found', how to check with the right ID and phone number, and when you need to submit a fresh application instead.

contentBlocks.title: No Records Found
contentBlocks.description: This is a matching problem, not a decision on your grant. SASSA could not link the details you entered to an application.

contentBlocks.text: When the status check cannot find an application, it returns 'No Records Found'. Nine times out of ten the cause is a mismatch: an ID digit typed incorrectly, a phone number that has changed, or an application that was started but never submitted. It does not mean you were declined and it does not mean you are blacklisted.

contentBlocks.explanation: The status lookup matches the ID number and the cellphone number you enter against the application record. If either differs by even one character, or if no complete application was ever saved, the system has nothing to display. Older applications that were closed or replaced also stop appearing.
whyItHappens: The ID number was typed with a wrong digit or the wrong document type was selected.
The phone number entered is not the number used on the application.
The application was started but never submitted, so no record was created.
The application was submitted under a different phone number or by an agent.
An older application was closed and a new one has not been submitted.
The record is still loading after a recent submission.
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: Until the correct details are used or a new application is submitted. It will not change on its own if no application exists.
whatYouShouldDo: Retry with your ID number exactly as printed, with no spaces.
Use the cellphone number that received the application SMS, not a new number.
Check your SMS inbox for a reference number — if you have one, the application exists.
If you applied through an agent or internet cafe, ask which phone number was used.
If no reference number exists, submit a fresh application and keep the confirmation.
If you are certain an application exists, call 0800 60 10 11 or visit an office with your ID.

contentBlocks.caption: Common causes of a no-record result

contentBlocks.title: No record is not a decline
contentBlocks.text: A decline is a decision that you did not qualify. No Records Found means SASSA has nothing to decide on. If you have no reference number, the practical answer is usually to apply again rather than keep checking.

contentBlocks.title: Be careful with agents
contentBlocks.text: Some internet cafes charge a fee and submit applications using their own phone number, which leaves you unable to check the status. Always ask for the reference number and make sure your own number is on the application.

faqs.question: Does No Records Found mean my grant was cancelled?
faqs.answer: No. It means no application could be matched to the details you entered. A cancelled grant would normally show a cancellation or inactive status.

faqs.question: I just applied. Why does it already say no records?
faqs.answer: New submissions can take a short while to appear, and sometimes a day or two over peak periods. Keep the reference number and check again.

faqs.question: Can I check with a different phone number?
faqs.answer: The lookup must use the number on the application. If you no longer have that SIM, visit an office to update the number before checking again.

faqs.question: Should I reapply if I already have a reference number?
faqs.answer: No. Reapplying with an existing reference can create a duplicate. Call 0800 60 10 11 or visit an office to trace the existing application.

faqs.question: Does this status affect my ID or credit record?
faqs.answer: No. It is only a grant application lookup result and has no effect on your ID, credit record or eligibility.
